claims: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch no earlier than Wednesday, April 1, 2026, at 6:24 p.m. EDT from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The Artemis II launch window is two hours.
Artemis II marks the first crewed mission to orbit the Moon in over 50 years.
Artemis II launch date is Wednesday, April 1, 2026.
Artemis II launch time is 6:24 p.m. EDT (22:24 UTC).
Artemis II launch window is 6:24 p.m. – 8:24 p.m. EDT.
Artemis II launch location is Launch Complex 39B, Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
Backup dates for Artemis II launch include April 2–6 and April 30 if necessary.
Live coverage of Artemis II will be available on NASA's YouTube channel.
Live coverage of Artemis II will be available on NASA+.
Coverage begins on the morning of April 1 with dedicated pre-launch coverage, according to Wired and ESA Web TV.
The Artemis II mission is a 10-day mission.
The Artemis II mission will test the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The Artemis II mission will test the Orion spacecraft.
The Artemis II mission has a crew of four astronauts.
